claims.text: Tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys are relevant to plasma-facing component applications.
Conventional melting produces a primarily disordered BCC structure in the proposed tungsten-based RHEA.
Stepwise controllable heat treatment can induce coherent nanoprecipitation in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed treatment will produce a well-dispersed nanoscale precipitate population.
Coherent nanoprecipitation will increase the effective thermal conductivity of the tungsten-based RHEA.
Coherent nanoprecipitation will preserve the alloy's high-temperature strength.
Coherent nanoprecipitation will preserve the alloy's high-temperature structural or thermal stability.
Crystallographically coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces reduce phonon and electron scattering relative to incoherent phase boundaries.
Reduced interfacial scattering increases phonon and electron mean free paths and thereby improves thermal transport.
The nanoprecipitates provide obstacles to dislocation motion that preserve high strength.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
SCCP processing can yield a tungsten RHEA with substantial strength and ductility, including high yield strength at 800 °C.
The combined thermal-conductivity and mechanical-integrity benefit will hold at temperatures of at least 800 °C.
The benefit will persist under sustained mechanical stress and cyclic thermal loading representative of reactor intermediate layers.
Current disordered single-phase BCC RHEA intermediate layers have suboptimal thermal transport because chemical disorder increases carrier scattering.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or precipitate volume fraction could degrade thermal conduction.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or precipitate volume fraction could embrittle the alloy.
The proposed benefit may be less effective below 800 °C.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant conductivity improvement, or significant degradation of yield strength or ductility relative to a conventionally processed control, would falsify the hypothesis.
